title: Eggs Benedict Hall Style
subtitle: Poached eggs, Canadian bacon, and hollandaise on toasted English muffins.
description: Poached eggs, Canadian bacon, and hollandaise on English muffins — hall-style benedict with a workflow that doesn't stall the whole kitchen.

steps.title: Make hollandaise
steps.instruction: Blend yolks, lemon juice, mustard, and a pinch of salt 30 seconds. With blender running on medium, slowly stream in hot melted butter until thick and glossy. Hold in a thermos or over a warm water bath—not direct heat.

steps.title: Toast muffins and warm bacon
steps.instruction: Split and toast English muffins at 350°F until edges are crisp, about 6 minutes. Warm Canadian bacon in a dry skillet over medium until lightly browned at the edges; hold covered on a warm tray.

steps.title: Set poaching water
steps.instruction: Bring two wide pots of water to a gentle simmer with a tablespoon of vinegar each—the surface should barely ripple, not roll. Crack each egg into a small cup before sliding into the water.

steps.title: Poach the eggs
steps.instruction: Slide eggs into simmering water one at a time. Poach 3–4 minutes until whites are fully set (165°F) and yolks remain runny. Lift with a slotted spoon, drain on paper towels, and trim ragged edges for clean plates.

steps.title: Assemble and sauce
steps.instruction: Place two muffin halves per plate, top each with bacon and a poached egg. Spoon hollandaise generously over each egg, finish with chives and lemon zest, and serve within 2 minutes while yolks are still liquid.

stationWorkflow: Make hollandaise first and hold warm—never reheat over direct flame or it will break.
Run two poaching pots in parallel so eight eggs finish within the same 4-minute window.
Toast muffins in batches right before poaching starts; cold muffins kill the dish on the plate.
cleanupNotes: Rinse poaching pots immediately with cold water so egg whites do not cook onto the sides.
Wash blender and whisk while hollandaise is still warm—set butter is miserable to scrub cold.
leftovers: Hollandaise does not reheat well; make a half batch if crew size is uncertain.
Use leftover Canadian bacon and muffins in a breakfast sandwich bake with scrambled eggs.
